sources.reason: Two single-event bug reports (a rare Wind Generating Band giving Sacred Shard and two Soul Dust, repeated by a second player) about Shadowlands materials from Dragonflight gear. No cast count, no input ID, and the note itself says they are not a study. The Serevite and Aqirite counts in the same file belong to reddit threads 10s9ol9 and 1g350pq.

One bug report of a Dragonflight rare staff giving two Large Brilliant Shards, a Classic reagent, with no input item ID or build. A single reported malfunction, not a measured cohort; the counts elsewhere in the file belong to other sources.

The thread is cited for a 2023 bug report (Prismatic Ore greyed out because the user had fewer than five ore). It states no outputs. The 400-ore / 80-cast superbondez numbers in the second file belong to wowhead item 194545, not to this thread.

The German hotfix article is only listed as a link (line 17). The cohort counts in the file (1,000 and 5,000 Titanium Ore, six gem totals each) belong to reddit s6bfrl and a Wowhead comment by Strath.

The workbook is cited for a formula audit. The quoted cells (F41=1.13, G41=0.38, H44=0.24) are the author's model coefficients, which the note says have no cast denominator or histogram. Not observations.

A secondary guide cited for two reagent ranks and specialisation-gated Diamond eligibility. The note calls it context, not a measured cohort; the counts nearby (Cardinalai 800 casts, JD3K 50 ore) are other sources.

The Milling herbs BFA sheet shows calculator defaults (1000 herbs, 310 Crimson, 130 Viridescent) that the note labels estimated quantities, not measured totals or cast observations. Modelled values, nothing to store as evidence.
Cited as a qualitative support for rarity-to-material families in disenchanting. The sample claims (12, 4, 3, 3, 1, 1) are GameData profile counts, not this page's results.
The page is the discovery link for the same Milling herbs BFA calculator sheet; its 1000 herbs / 310 / 130 figures are labelled estimates and calculator defaults, not observations.
A 2023 anecdote recalling ('IIRC') that skill 250 guarantees rank-3 pigment. No cast, count or output total; the note says it is not a completed-cast study.

A crafting spreadsheet post. The numbers in the note are the sheet's formula cells and talent coefficients (Shuffles!F41=1.13, H44=0.24 and so on), which the note describes as hardcoded model values, not sampled results.

A 2024 milling calculator post, called a model lead by both notes: no cast histogram and no exact output totals. The 11 to 17 and 9 to 13 pigment ranges in the files belong to other threads (1ey4dkl, 1fb0vv5).
Reports that R2 gems are about 8 percent more valuable than R1, with no sample denominator or price snapshot. A value claim, no counts of outputs; the note says direct retrieval was blocked.
Reports a gold profitability result (about 42,000g input, under 32,000g returned) with no ore count, no output ledger and no casts; the note says not to import its implied return.
A March 2026 discussion that reports rank-2 glass from skilled rank-2 ore in words. The note says it establishes no ore ID, probability or count.
An April 2026 discussion that reports rank-2 stone and glass in words, with no ore ID, count or probability.

A commenter reports 35 to 40 dust after 1,000 ore. The result is a range of totals, the method is crushing rather than one of the four methods, and the note itself says gross ore is not a cast count and the gem and rank are unknown. Null on doubt.
Two player comments about profitability (losses with max talents; rank-one profitable, rank-two intermittent). The note says no cast denominator or item histogram; qualitative and price dependent.

The post is named only as a TSM-string repost derived from the 2020 original, which both notes suppressed as a duplicate. Every count in these files belongs to other sources (Jiyao, Hochenblume, First Flower, Titanium).

A commenter references a chart from 3,300 Laestrite mass prospects, but the chart's outputs are not in the files and the note records it as NEEDS_RECHECK with zero numerical credit. The original post is needed.
Taken from the source-only archive note, which gives the item IDs and the post date; the batch013 report in the queue states the same three totals. No cast count is stated, so casts stay null.

The note gives 10,000 ore and about 0.7% 'per essence' for Progenium PTR and 3.5% against a reported 2.7% for Elethium. The output is not named (which essence), the percentage is approximate with no meaning stated, and the Elethium figures are not attributed to a cohort. The note calls it a lead, not a numeric study.

The thread is cited as a TSM user discussion of whether amountOfMats is per herb. The Peacebloom, Mageroyal and Earthroot cast histograms in the same file are the Wowhead commenter 180977's PTR cohorts, a different source.

The Prospect Me table is named only as identity corroboration for the milling table. The counts in the file (2,000 herbs of each of six species; 1,000 herbs per cohort; over 100,000 herbs) belong to Wowhead comments 516803, Kidneph, Baadkitty and Melch1337.

A 2015 ReagentMaker data file whose values the note calls authored data-table assumptions, not measured evidence; the file's numbers are not quoted. The Peacebloom and Mageroyal histograms nearby are a different source.

The October 27 hotfix page is cited because it gives no applicable numeric prospecting rate. The counts in the file (10,000 R2 Aqirite, 800 Silver casts) belong to reddit 1g350pq and Cardinalai's comment.

The Czech guide says crushing three identical gems gives one to three Glimmering Gemdust. That is a family-level range from a secondary guide, for a crushing recipe that is not one of the four methods, and the note says it is not a completed-cast sample. Null on doubt.

Cited as derivative context for the Felslate and Leystone comparison. The counts in the file (143 powder from 1,000 ore, 177 casts) belong to a Wowhead comment by globalmenace and to held mass-milling rows.

Describes a general 30 percent reagent-return heuristic, which the note calls a secondary explanation and not a measured distribution. The counts nearby (10,000 Serevite, 11,000 R1 / 10,000 R2 Aqirite) belong to reddit 10s9ol9 and 1g350pq.

The guide is cited for its item-level brackets. The 288-cast counts (217 casts giving 554 essences, 71 giving 234 dust) belong to the original Wowhead comments on items 52719 and 52555, not to the guide.

The review note says the guide gives six Pyrite common gem chances of 17% each, but does not name the gems or ranks, and the table itself is not in the files. A reference row would have no identifiable output.

The review note gives 'common 24%, rare 5%, Trillium 17%' for the guide, but not which items or ranks each figure covers, and the guide's table is not in the files. The Kyparite cohort figures in the same bullet are unattributed per-ore aggregates.

The guide link supports Bubble Poppy and Writhebark to pigment identity and '5 herbs per mill'. It names no recipe spell and no result, so there is no recipe or drop row to extract; the 2 to 5 yield is a guide statement.

A 2017 comment on the Felslate page 'mixes 880 Leystone and 240 Felslate' in one report, so the gem yields cannot be tied to Felslate alone. The 10,000-ore worksheet figures are a different source (Scribd).
